name: Frankel
one_line: Ran 14 races, won all 14, and retired as the highest-rated racehorse in the history of ratings.

facts.claim: raced 14 times between 2010 and 2012 and won all 14, retiring unbeaten
facts.note: British thoroughbred, owned by Khalid Abdullah, sired by Galileo, named after the late American trainer Bobby Frankel.

facts.claim: rated 147 by Timeform - the highest rating in the organisation's history, ahead of Sea-Bird's 145 (1965)
facts.note: Timeform has rated racehorses since 1948. Chart: gold 147 vs gray 145 - and note Sea-Bird's 145 stood for ~47 years as the ceiling. Wikipedia confirms 'highest-rated horse in the organisation's history.'

facts.claim: won the 2011 2000 Guineas by six lengths, described as 'one of the greatest displays on a British racecourse'
facts.note: He led almost the entire race - commentators thought the jockey had lost control; the horse was just faster than the sport.

facts.claim: bookmakers priced him as short as 1/20 - bet twenty to win one
facts.note: Sussex Stakes 2012. Betting on him became nearly pointless - the market gave up pretending he could lose.

facts.claim: his trainer, Sir Henry Cecil, trained Frankel's entire career while dying of cancer; he said a 2012 win made him feel 'twenty years better'; he died in June 2013, months after Frankel retired
facts.note: The human heart of the video. Cecil was a legendary trainer in decline - written off by the sport - and Frankel was his resurrection. Report flat.

facts.claim: retired to stud at a fee of 125,000 pounds per mating, which rose to 350,000 by 2024
facts.note: The only athlete on this channel whose retirement job pays six figures per appointment.

comparison.second_label: the best of every other horse since 1948
comparison.gap_description: 147 against 145 - a ceiling that had stood for half a century, cleared.

story_beat: His trainer, Sir Henry Cecil, was a racing legend the sport had written off, and he was dying of cancer. Frankel gave him fourteen wins in fourteen races on the way out - Cecil said one of them made him feel twenty years better. He died months after the horse retired.
